category_title: Gifted girls with ADHD experiencing organizational failure and academic anxiety
minimal_context: The student is attempting to complete a large volume of Algebra 2 homework.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at your Algebra 2 homework. You have a lot of problems to finish today.

STUDENT: I was struggling. I just wasn't getting what he said at all. Since I was GT, most of the kids got stuff faster than me, so I wouldn't really get the material.

TUTOR: Just keep trying. Let's work on the next section.

STUDENT: I spend a lot of time doing homework or attempting to do homework. There's a lot of time spent not doing homework but not doing anything else either because I still have homework to do, if that makes sense.

TUTOR: You just need to focus and get it done so you can turn it in.

STUDENT: He gave out a lot of homework that I couldn't really finish and if I did, I forgot to turn it in so I got marked off a lot for that. I wanted to cry.

options.A: Implement a daily point system, with the student's daily goal set at earning 80% of the possible points each day.
options.B: Implement prevention efforts focused on creating a warm and responsive climate and teaching positive bystander roles.
options.C: Provide opportunities for choice in Algebra 2 homework assignments and related projects throughout the term.
options.D: Hold back from providing answers immediately, using careful questioning to respond to student thinking and emphasize conceptual connections.
